company.description: The company name as given in the input.

studio_archetype.description: One short phrase: founder-led boutique, DP-led, production company, agency, huge production company, or unknown. Prefer "production company" over "unknown" whenever the evidence (including the company name itself) supports it - see the reasoning ladder.

operating_model.description: The business's organizational/ownership structure - not a client-relationship fact, and not a restatement of studio_archetype. "Works with multiple clients" is not a structure; "Owner-operated" is. UNKNOWN only if the reasoning ladder is fully exhausted.

studio_personality.description: 1-3 tags from the closed vocabulary describing how you'd work with them day to day. Empty array only if the reasoning ladder is fully exhausted.

creative_dna.description: 1-3 tags from the closed vocabulary answering: what kind of creative work excites them? A genuine creative specialty, not a restatement of what their clients happen to sell. Empty array if none genuinely fit - this one stays conservative, since a wrong genre tag is worse than none.

visual_dna.description: 1-3 tags from the closed vocabulary describing the actual look - the vocabulary a colorist would use to start a grade. Empty array if none genuinely fit - this one stays conservative, since a wrong look tag is worse than none.

decision_maker.description: ROLE only, no name - the CRM already has the contact's name, and role is what actually changes the outreach. Compress a messy real-world title into a clean short label: "Business & creative director and owner" -> "Owner/Creative Director", "Writer | Producer" -> "Writer/Producer". UNKNOWN only if no title at all is given.

buyer_personality.description: 1-3 tags from the closed vocabulary on how they evaluate and decide. Empty array only if the reasoning ladder is fully exhausted.

most_distinctive_insight.description: The single most distinctive thing about who this company is - not necessarily something rare or unusual, just the strongest available insight. Follow the reasoning ladder: a unique detail beats a meaningful one, a meaningful one beats the plain business model, and the plain business model beats UNKNOWN. UNKNOWN is a last resort, not a default. A few words, not a sentence. Never a generic compliment ("award-winning", "passionate").

colorkaar_angle.description: A short punchy phrase, roughly 3-8 words, on why Colorkaar specifically matters here. Not a sentence that explains itself with an em-dash. Not an email.

conversation_starter.description: An actual question a producer would ask and expect a reply to - not a topic label. One natural sentence, specific to this company. e.g. "How do you approach maintaining a consistent look across branded campaigns?" not "Grading for branded campaigns." This is the one field exempt from the compression rule's word-count guidance - it needs to read as a real question, not a phrase.

avoid.description: Actionable writing constraints for whoever drafts the email, as short imperative directives - e.g. ["Don't lead with pricing", "Don't mention luxury clients", "Don't use generic storytelling compliments"]. Not bare tags. Free text - situational, not a closed vocabulary.

why_this_lead.description: 3-5 short bullets synthesizing the case for outreach - the gut-check a producer reads before deciding whether to write at all. Can reuse tags from other fields plus specific facts. e.g. ["Founder-led", "Image-first", "No internal grading", "Relationship-driven"].

outreach_priority.description: Your proposed priority tier. Recomputed deterministically downstream from studio_archetype and evidence_strength - reason honestly.

evidence_strength.description: How much of this profile rests on facts stated directly in the evidence (including the company name) versus reasonable inference. NOT a measure of how interesting or complete the profile is - a Weak-evidence profile can and should still have real values in every field, just clearly built on inference rather than direct statement. Strong: most fields come from facts stated directly. Moderate: a real mix of stated fact and inference. Weak: almost everything is inferred from thin signal (a name, a title, a one-line description).

reasoning.description: Debug only, dropped before export. Briefly separate what was FACT (stated directly), what was INFERENCE (reasoned from that fact), and what was the resulting INSIGHT - e.g. "Fact: description says 'production company', 'directors' cuts'. Inference: works across multiple client types, not a single-brand in-house team. Insight: directors'-cuts specialist."
